items.text: Code convention (user's rule, stated 2026-11-03): never use positional boolean parameters; options must be passed via an options object, e.g. `parse(str, { requireUnit: true })`, not `parse(x, true)`, because a positional boolean tells you nothing at the call site. If `requireUnit` is added to `ms()` or `parseStrict()`, it should go in the existing `Options` interface, which already carries `long`.

The `parse` function in src/index.ts accepts an optional options object `ParseOptions = { requireUnit?: boolean }`, added 2026-11-03 (uncommitted in the working tree at the time). With `{ requireUnit: true }`, unitless strings such as '30', '-1.5' and '.5' return NaN; default behaviour is unchanged (`parse('30')` still returns 30). Motivation: bare numbers in config files are read as milliseconds, which is almost always a mistake. `requireUnit` exists only on `parse`; `ms()` and `parseStrict()` do not take it yet. Jest (171 tests, 100% coverage), tsc and biome passed.

items.text: In 2025 ms (vercel/ms) was modernized toward a new major version (4.x) with breaking changes: ESM-only output and dropping Node 18 (#264), removal of the default export (#267, after it was briefly added back in #259), `ms` moved to a named export (#243, closes #237), IE support dropped with lint fixes (#244, closes #236), and minimum Node raised to 18 (#226). Node 16 was too old to upgrade tools like pnpm, jest and husky (learned in #224), so Node had to be updated first. Work ran July 29 - August 27, 2025, by Dimitri Mitropoulos and Steven.

The ms library (time-string/milliseconds conversion) was imported as a repository by Guillermo Rauch on 2012-03-07; on 2012-03-08 tubalmartin contributed a rewrite with a smaller footprint and 2.8x better performance that passed all unit tests.
